fleetMemory.LESSON: A function returning `null` for 'modelled', 'declined' and 'unreached' at once does not merely lose detail -- it forces every caller to guess, and the guess becomes a customer-facing sentence. Here THREE separate call sites guessed (the bake's token outranking the attempt, the stub's `?? "atom_path_pending"` default, and the route gate that skipped the attempt entirely) and all three produced the SAME false claim, which is why one defect looked like three dispatch sites and was one design fault.

Do not leave the reason's default at the LAST composer in the chain. `reason: envelopeRefusalReason ?? "atom_path_pending"` meant 'if I was told nothing, I assert the setbacks are unruled'. Making the input a required non-null `string` converts 'a surface can invent this' into 'a surface must be handed this'; the type is the enforcement, and F5 above is a TYPE assertion, not a runtime one, so it must not be sold as more than that.

Before removing a customer-facing token, check whether it is in an instrument's phrase list -- and which class that feeds. `atom_path_pending` sits in GEOMETRY_REFUSAL_PHRASES, which only fires when the probe saw geometry DRAWN, so removing the token from the MCP text clears BOTH the rule class (via 'unruled' in the rendered sentence) and the geometry class. Two classes, one string, two different predicates -- the class you think you are fixing may not be the only one the string trips.
